question.problem:
If $B$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and $\text{rank}(B-2I)=3,$ which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{nullity}(B-2I)=1$

II. $B-2I$ is non-singular

III. $\lambda =2$ is an eigenvalue of $B$
question.worked_solution:
Given a $4\times 4$ matrix $M,$ we have the following by the invertible matrix theorem:

$M$ is invertible $\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(M)={R}^{4} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(M))=4=\text{rank}(M) \\  & \text{Null}(M)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(M))=0=\text{nullity}(M)\end{aligned}$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $M$ has $4$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(M)+\text{nullity}(M)=4.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. According to the rank-nullity theorem, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{nullity}(B-2I) & =4-\text{rank}(B-2I) \\  & =4-3 \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

- Statements II is false. By the invertible matrix theorem, since $\text{nullity}(B-2I)\ne 0,$ we obtain that $B-2I$ must be singular.

- Statement III is true. Notice that if $M=B-2I$ is singular, then $(B-2I)x=0$ has nonzero solutions which will be eigenvectors of $B.$ As a result, $\lambda =2$ is an eigenvalue of $B.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
